title: Cycle remote execute/wait on unresponsive end

timeline.body:

server termination. Ignore this state and rewait for the execution

Cycle remote execute/wait on unresponsive end

If an execute/waitExecution stream ends, it can be the result of a
server termination. Ignore this state and rewait for the execution
assuming we are configured to do so.

Why do you feel you need to use an infinite loop as opposed to handling this in the retrier?

reply.body: Because the completion is not an innate exception, and shouldn't count against the retry limit. The existing request behavior - waiting if necessary without a deadline, forever - indicates that a completion doesn't represent an error condition, and that only request exceptions can represent transiency worth retrying and expending retry attempts.
Apologies for my comment I was thinking of a different problem that you are trying to fix. Makes total sense. May I ask you to add a test so that we don't regress on it?

timeline.message: Test to verify unfinished execute completed cycle
